title: Songhai & Timbuktu (Tarikh es-Soudan), Futuh Misr, Arabian Ariba/Qahtan/Adnan, Ludolf Ethiopia & Palmyra/Zenobia

nodes.name: Za-Al-Ayaman ('Came from Yemen' → Kukya on the Niger) → 14 Pre-Islamic Za Kings → Za-Kosoi (1st Muslim King of Songhai, 1009 CE)
nodes.era: Early Niger Bend → 1010 CE (Tarikh es-Soudan Ch. 1 pp. 35-38)
nodes.role: Yemeni-Originated Founder of the Songhai Za Dynasty on the Niger
sources: Abderrahman es-Sa'di Tarikh es-Soudan (tr. Houdas 1900) Ch. 1 pp. 35-38
nodes.notes: Tarikh es-Soudan derives the royal Za (Dia) dynasty of Kukya/Songhai from two brothers who traveled from Yemen ('dja men el-Yemen' -> Za-Al-Ayaman), slaying the pagan river-idol and ruling through 14 pre-Islamic kings until Za-Kosoi (Moslem-dam) embraced Islam in AH 400 (1009-1010 CE).

nodes.name: Songhai Empire & Timbuktu: Sonni Ali-Kolon → Sonni Ali (1464) → Askia El-Hadj Mohammed (Askia the Great, 1493)
nodes.role: Imperial Sultans of Gao & Timbuktu Following Mali Supremacy
sources: Abderrahman es-Sa'di Tarikh es-Soudan (tr. Houdas 1900) Ch. 2-3 pp. 39-44
nodes.notes: Brothers Ali-Kolon and Selman-Nar (sons of Za-Yasiboy) freed Songhai from Mansa Musa's Mali suzerainty, inaugurating the Sonni line culminating in Sonni Ali before Askia El-Hadj Mohammed (the Great, 1493) elevated Timbuktu and Songhai.

nodes.name: Futuh Misr (Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam): 'Amr ibn al-'As (Egypt), Uqba ibn Nafi (Maghreb) & Tariq ibn Ziyad (Al-Andalus, 711 CE)
nodes.era: 7th–8th c. CE (Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam Futuh Misr, Torrey ed.)
nodes.role: Earliest Arabic Chronicle of Egypt, Berbers of North Africa & Al-Andalus
sources: Ibn 'Abd al-Hakam Futuh Misr (ed. C.C. Torrey, Yale Oriental Series III)
nodes.notes: Earliest extant Arabic historical narrative covering 'Amr ibn al-'As's Coptic treaty in Egypt (Misr), Uqba ibn Nafi's campaigns across the Amazigh/Berber Maghreb, and Tariq ibn Ziyad & Musa ibn Nusayr's 711 CE crossing into Visigothic Spain.

nodes.name: Ancient Arabian Ariba (Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1): Cushites of Arabia, 'Ad (Loqman) & Amaliqa / Samayda of Ayla
nodes.era: Pre-Islamic Antiquity (Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1 pp. 21-39)
nodes.role: Extinct Ancient Arabian Tribes Bridged to Cush, Uz/Aram & Ham
sources: Caussin de Perceval Essai sur l'Histoire des Arabes Vol. 1 (1847) pp. 21-39
nodes.notes: Caussin de Perceval synthesizes Jewish and classical Arab genealogies (Ibn Sa'id, Ibn Habib, Tabari) tracing the primitive Arab al-'Ariba — Cushites along the Arabian peninsula, 'Ad (Uz b. Aram / Amalek b. Ham, including Loqman of the Seven Vultures), and the Samayda Amaliqa of Ayla.

nodes.name: Pre-Islamic Arabian Tribal Tree (Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1): Qahtan (Himyar, Kahlan, Azd, Kindah) & Adnan (Ma'add → Nizar → Mudar & Rabi'a)
nodes.era: Bronze Age → 6th c. CE (Caussin de Perceval Vol. 1 pp. 23-39+)
nodes.role: Complete Bifurcation of Southern Qahtanite & Northern Adnanite Arab Confederations
sources: Caussin de Perceval Essai sur l'Histoire des Arabes Vol. 1 (1847) pp. 23-39+
nodes.notes: Maps the dual trunk of Arabian ethnogenesis: Southern Al-'Ariba / Mutariba descending from Qahtan (Joktan b. Eber -> Ya'rub -> Himyar, Kahlan, Azd, Ghassan, Lakhm & Kindah) and Northern Musta'riba descending from Ishmael via Adnan -> Ma'add -> Nizar -> Mudar & Rabi'a.

nodes.name: Ludolf's Ethiopian-Himyarite War (1684): King Kaleb (Elesbaan) vs. Dhu Nuwas, Abreha & Saif ibn Dhi Yazan (+ Khosrow I Anushirvan)
sources: Hiob Ludolf A New History of Ethiopia (1684) pp. 166-167
nodes.notes: Ludolf chronicles King Kaleb (Caleb / Elesbaan) of Aksum avenging the Christian martyrs of Najran against Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas, placing Abreha in Yemen until Himyarite prince Saif ibn Dhi Yazan regained Yemen with Sasanian Emperor Khosrow I Anushirvan's aid.

nodes.name: Gondar Solomonic Emperors (Ludolf 1684): Lebna Dengel → Galawdewos → Emperor Susenyos → Emperor Fasilides (Founder of Gondar, 1632)
nodes.role: Renaissance & Early Modern Ethiopian Solomonic Sovereign Succession
sources: Hiob Ludolf A New History of Ethiopia (1684)
nodes.notes: Continues the Ethiopian Solomonic line documented in Ludolf's 1684 chronicle from Lebna Dengel (Dawit II) and Galawdewos (Claudius) through Emperor Susenyos I and his son Emperor Fasilides, who established the royal capital at Gondar in 1632.

nodes.name: Palmyra / Tadmor (Seller 1696): Founded by King Solomon → Nabataean King Aretas (Al-Harith of Ghassan / Petra)
nodes.role: Solomonic Foundation of Tadmor & Arab-Nabataean Princes of Syria
sources: Abednego Seller The Antiquities of Palmyra (1696) Preface
nodes.notes: Seller (1696) links ancient Palmyra directly to Biblical Tadmor fortified by King Solomon in the Syrian desert, tracing subsequent Arabian mastery from Nabataean king Aretas (equated by Seller with the Al-Harith rulers of Petra and Ghassan, contemporary of Pompey c. 63 BCE).

nodes.name: Palmyrene Empire (Seller 1696): King Odenathus → Queen Zenobia (Claiming Descent from Cleopatra VII & Dido) & Vaballathus
nodes.role: Palmyrene Imperial House Claiming Ptolemaic & Phoenician Royal Bloodlines
sources: Abednego Seller The Antiquities of Palmyra (1696)
nodes.notes: Seller details the rise of Palmyra under Septimius Odaenathus ('King of Kings') and his learned queen Zenobia Bat-Zabbai — who claimed royal ancestry from Egypt's Cleopatra VII and Carthaginian Dido while ruling Syria, Egypt & Anatolia before Aurelian's triumph.
